title: Environment Variables and Configuration knowledge check

questions.prompt: What should a reliable TypeScript integration do with external data?
options: Validate data and failures at runtime, while using types to make trusted application contracts explicit.
Assume the declared type validates the server response.
Ignore promise rejections and malformed data.
Treat JSON.parse as a validation step.
questions.answer_key: Validate data and failures at runtime, while using types to make trusted application contracts explicit.
questions.explanation: Types and runtime validation solve different problems at external boundaries.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Environment Variables and Configuration”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with environment variable declarations and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with environment variable declarations and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Environment variable declarations”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Environment Variables and Configuration”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check string-valued configuration, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume parsing and validating configuration at runtime is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check string-valued configuration, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “String-valued configuration”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
